newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb hits train near Algiers, kills 21.
newsitem.headline: Bomb hits train near Algiers, kills 21.

text.p: Twenty-one people were killed and 20 others wounded on Friday when a bomb exploded beside a train passing through a station near Algiers, Algerian security forces said.

The official news agency APS, quoting a security forces statement, said the explosion occured when a passenger train was passing near Oued El Kerma at 8 a.m. (0700 GMT). It described the blast as "a criminal act", which usually refers to attacks by Algeria's Islamist rebels.

"The bomb, which was planted under the railway at Oued El Kerma, completely destroyed the first coach of the train and killed 21 people, including three women," a witness to the damage told Reuters over the telephone.
Among the 20 wounded passengers, who were transported to the neighbouring hospital, three men were badly wounded, he added.
The train links the Algiers suburb of Khemiss Meliana to the capital, a resident of Oued Kerma said, adding the train was not full because it was a Friday, the weekend in Algeria.
"The bomb made a seven-metre (yd) large crater...The traffic was suspended on the train line between Khemiss Meliana and Algiers," he said. Khemiss Meliana is 100 km (60 miles) south of Algiers.
It was not known if "the criminals" behind the blast, were arrested or not, he said.
Early this month a bomb exploded in a market near Blida, 50 km south of Algiers, killing eight people and wounding 26 others, the resident added.
